name: research retrospective after E11-E13
hypothesis: After 4 experiments (E11-E13 + first RETRO), re-examine patterns, Goodhart risks, and adversarial falsification to re-rank the experiment queue.
notes: 3 parallel independent subagents: (1) patterns — deterministic changes win, add-more-context regresses, measure-instrument-fix works; (2) Goodhart — coverage is mention-frequency proxy, hallucination is symbol-existence only, broken-examples 6.2% is largely self-inflicted via E13's <REQUIRED> placeholders (19 across 9/11 e2e pages, 10/13 residual findings), grounded-claims is a repetition-count; (3) adversarial — 7 source-verified factual errors in prose/tables, ALL missed by current checkers (method-vs-property confusion, return-type mismatches, arg-type mismatches, cross-page inconsistency). Key decisions: E13b (fix placeholder) promoted to NEXT; E18 (prose API semantics checker) promoted to second; E14 re-scoped with 2x-band threshold (4.2pp coverage, 24 grounded) and post-surgical placeholder-aware broken% as co-primary metric; add placeholder_value finding type to example_check.py; rename hallucination_rate to invented_symbol_rate. name: fix REQUIRED placeholder with value inference
hypothesis: Replacing E13's <REQUIRED> placeholder with a valid inferred value (from sibling kwargs or AST default) or omitting the kwarg with an annotation will make the broken-examples metric honest and eliminate the metric-gaming artifact.
changes: repoquill/surgical_verify.py: build_class_index now captures init_defaults (ast.unparse of default values); new _infer_value() function (Rule 1: AST default, Rule 2: judge_X mirrors X, Rule 3: provider mirrors judge_provider); _fix_missing_required_in_block uses _infer_value instead of inserting <REQUIRED>; _normalize_quotes for consistent double-quote style; trailing-comma detection to avoid double commas
/tmp/rq-trials/harness/example_check.py: new placeholder_value finding type; _is_placeholder() checks for <REQUIRED>, TODO, FIXME, PLACEHOLDER, ..., <value>, <arg>, <name> sentinel values
notes: BROKEN EXAMPLES: 13.8% mean (3 runs: 11.8, 21.2, 8.5) vs E13's 6.2%. The increase is HONEST — E13's <REQUIRED> placeholder satisfied the checker's missing_required test, hiding the true broken rate. E13b's inferred values are valid and runnable (e.g. judge_provider='ollama' when provider='ollama'). 0 placeholders across all 3 runs (vs 19 in E13). Remaining findings are missing_required (genuinely missing params the LLM didn't include) and occasional invalid_kwarg/syntax_error — these are GENERATION problems for E14 to address, not surgical verify problems. Coverage Run 1 (61.3%) is an outlier; Runs 2-3 (70.7%, 71.7%) are at or above baseline. Decision: KEEP — eliminates metric-gaming, coverage within 2x band, hallucination unchanged, grounded slightly higher.

hypothesis: A semantic value checker that flags (a) string literal values in code blocks that are strict prefixes/abbreviations of the source parameter's default, and (b) method calls with known runtime caveats that are not mentioned in the page, will catch the 2 HIGH-severity C-hallucination errors identified by RETRO3 (language='en' vs 'English', missing event-loop RuntimeError caveat) without false positives.
experiment: Built eval/semantic_value_check.py with 2 checks: STRING_VALUE_MISMATCH (global param-name -> defaults map, prefix/abbreviation heuristic) and MISSING_CAVEAT (global method-name -> caveats map, key-phrase matching). Validated against E14 and E19 docs.

Generic design (param-name-agnostic and method-name-agnostic) works for any repo. Confirms RETRO3 secondary check: grounding pass (E19) cannot fix these errors because they are outside the prose checker's finding types.
limitations: Prefix/abbreviation heuristic may miss non-prefix value errors (e.g. language='French' when default is 'English')
Caveat key-phrase list is fixed (event loop, RuntimeError, active event, thread, asyncio) — may miss other runtime condition patterns
Only checks fenced code blocks for string values, not inline code

design: 4 variants × 3 runs: A (temp 0.1, max 20 = E19 config), B (temp 0.0, max 20), C (temp 0.1, max 5), D (temp 0.0, max 5). All prose-only grounding (no semantic checker).
rationale: No variant beats E19 on all metrics simultaneously. B (temp 0.0) has best prose (1.3) and coverage (55.1%) but broken 13.9% (E19: 5.2%). C/D (max 5) have terrible prose (21.7/22.7) — limiting findings makes the LLM fix fewer issues. A (same config as E19) has broken 9.1% vs E19's 5.2% — this is base-generation variance, not a grounding-pass effect. Key insight: dominant broken-example failure mode is syntax_error from API signature snippets (legitimate documentation pattern, not actually broken). This is a Goodharting concern: the metric counts signature snippets as 'broken' when they're not really broken. Code changes (grounding_temperature, grounding_max_findings, grounding_semantic config options) KEPT for future experiments.

hypothesis: Fixing the example checker to exclude API signature snippets (which are legitimate documentation, not executable code) will reduce the broken-examples rate without affecting generation quality.
changes: eval/example_check.py: added _is_signature_block() to detect and skip API signature snippets (Name(...) or Name.Name(...) patterns with type annotations that fail to parse as valid Python)
rationale: Checker fix is correct (properly excludes signature snippets — no syntax_error findings in E25 runs), but E25's broken% (13.5% mean) is WORSE than E19 (4.2% mean) with the same fixed checker. The high broken% is a real quality issue: the LLM is generating genuinely broken examples (property_called_as_method, missing_required, invalid_kwarg). The checker fix doesn't improve generation quality — it only makes the metric more honest. Coverage also regressed (51.2% vs 54.6%).
next: Investigate why E25 runs have more broken examples than E19. Possible causes: (1) grounding pass is introducing errors, (2) LLM variance, (3) config differences. Consider running E19 config without grounding pass to isolate the variable.

hypothesis: Running E19 config WITHOUT grounding pass will isolate whether the grounding pass introduces broken examples. If broken% drops significantly without grounding → grounding pass is the cause of E25's regression. If broken% is similar → LLM variance.
rationale: E26 (WITHOUT grounding) has broken% = 15.2% — WORSE than E25 (WITH grounding, 13.5%) and E19 (WITH grounding, 4.2%). The grounding pass is NOT the cause of the broken-example regression. The dominant error type is property_called_as_method (13/14 findings in r1) — the LLM consistently calls @property attributes as methods. Root cause: extract_api_surface() lists ALL FunctionDef items as 'methods' without checking for @property decorators, so the LLM sees score() in the API surface and correctly calls it as a method. E27 will fix this.
next: E27: Mark @property attributes in API surface extraction + add prompt rule.

hypothesis: Marking @property attributes as PROPERTIES (not methods) in the API surface extraction, plus adding a prompt rule to use them as attributes, will eliminate the dominant property_called_as_method broken-example type.

repoquill/narrative.py: Added rule 7 to strict prompt: PROPERTIES are attributes, NOT methods. Use them as obj.name, never as obj.name()
rationale: property_called_as_method = 0 in 3/3 runs (was the dominant error type in E25/E26). Broken% 3.5% (E19: 4.2%, E25: 13.5%, E26: 15.2%). Coverage 55.1% (E19: 54.6%, within 4.2pp band). Halluc 0.0% (E19: 0.3%). Remaining broken findings are syntax_error (5 total across 3 runs) from legitimate code blocks, not property calls. Generic fix — any Python package with @property benefits.

hypothesis: The 5 remaining syntax_error findings across E27 runs are from code blocks with leading indentation (a formatting artifact), not genuine code errors. Stripping leading indentation from code blocks before syntax-checking will eliminate the spurious findings.

This strips leading indentation that the LLM sometimes adds to the entire code block (including the fence), which causes a spurious "unexpected indent" syntax error at line 1.
rationale: De-Goodhart fix: the metric now measures code correctness, not markdown formatting. All 5 syntax_error findings were from indented code blocks (formatting artifact), not genuine code errors. The remaining 1 missing_required finding in E27_r2 is a genuine error (AuditExperiment() missing 'models' param). Broken% drops from 3.5% to 0.7% mean. No generation change — evaluation infrastructure only.

next: E32: Build claim-verification checker for C-hallucination metric.

hypothesis: The C-hallucination rate (doc references REAL symbol but asserts FALSE fact) has never been measured. Building a claim-verification checker that extracts atomic type claims from prose and verifies them against AST extraction will establish a baseline.
changes: eval/claim_verification_check.py: NEW checker. build_claim_index() extracts class fields/methods/properties from AST. extract_claims() uses regex to find TYPE_CLAIM, RETURN_CLAIM, ASYNC_CLAIM patterns in prose. verify_claims() validates each claim against the index, classifies SUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED/UNVERIFIABLE. Compatible pairs: (int,float), (float,int), (str,string).
rationale: New metric established. 18.8% C-hallucination rate is the first measurement of this failure mode. The 3 contradicted claims are: expected_behavior claimed 'list' but is Optional[List[str]] (x2 runs), failed claimed 'bool' but is int (1 run). These are confident-but-wrong type claims — the LLM is making specific type assertions that are factually incorrect. This is a higher-severity failure mode than S-hallucination (invented symbols) because the symbol exists but the fact is wrong.
next: E33: Reduce C-hallucination rate via prompt change. Hypothesis: LLM makes confident but wrong type claims. Test if adding a prompt rule encouraging conservatism about type claims reduces the rate.

hypothesis: The 18.8% C-hallucination rate is driven by the LLM making confident but wrong type claims. Adding a prompt rule that encourages conservatism about type claims will reduce the rate by >=5pp without regressing other metrics.
changes: repoquill/narrative.py: added rule 8 to strict prompt: 'When describing the type of a field, parameter, or return value, ONLY state the type if it is explicitly annotated in the source code. If the source shows Optional[List[str]], write an optional list of strings — do NOT simplify to a list. If no annotation is present, describe the value without asserting a specific type.'
rationale: C-hallucination dropped 5.9pp (18.8% → 12.9%), barely above the 5pp threshold. However, hallucination regressed (+0.33pp: 0.7% → 1.03%) and broken examples regressed (+2.2pp: 0.7% → 2.9%). The prompt rule added noise without a clear net benefit. The C-hallucination rate is likely driven by LLM variance rather than a fixable prompt issue. The 3 contradicted claims in E27 (expected_behavior claimed 'list' but Optional[List[str]] x2, failed claimed 'bool' but int) are specific type assertions that the LLM makes confidently but incorrectly. action.root_cause: The LLM infers passed/failed return type from the method name (passed -> bool, failed -> bool) rather than the -> int annotation. This is a fundamental LLM reasoning pattern that a single prompt rule cannot override. The annotation IS visible in the source code (results.py line 167: def passed(self) -> int), but the LLM ignores it in favor of the name-based inference. Possible future approaches: (1) deterministic post-processing that checks type claims against AST annotations and corrects them, (2) inject a 'TYPE ANNOTATIONS' section that explicitly lists return types for all public methods, (3) accept this as a known limitation.
